set_title: Painful urination or fever with pus in the urine: urethra, bladder, prostate or kidney
stem: A 49-year-old man has had 2 days of fever to 39.0°C, chills, burning with urination and pain between the scrotum and anus. On rectal examination the prostate is exquisitely tender, warm and boggy. Urinalysis shows numerous white cells and bacteria.
oneliner: 49M + 2 days of fever 39.0 + chills + dysuria + perineal pain + tender boggy prostate + pyuria and bacteria → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.A: Pyelonephritis causes flank pain and costovertebral angle tenderness; he has **perineal pain and a tender prostate**
whyNot.B: Urethritis gives discharge and a sterile culture without high fever; he has **fever of 39.0°C and bacteria in the urine**
whyNot.C: Cystitis has little fever and a normal prostate; he has **fever and a boggy, tender prostate**
whyNot.E: An abscess causes flank pain with persistent fever; he has **perineal pain** and a **tender prostate**

why: Bacteria ascend the urethra or reflux into the prostatic ducts. **Fever with perineal pain and an exquisitely tender, boggy prostate** is acute bacterial prostatitis, caused by Escherichia coli in older men and by Chlamydia or gonococcus in younger men.

Women of reproductive age; pregnancy (ureteral dilation and stasis), diabetes, reflux
Dysuria with urethral discharge; no fever or flank pain
**Pyuria with a sterile routine urine culture** (Chlamydia trachomatis does not grow on routine media)
Sexually active adolescents and young adults

Pyuria and bacteria; Escherichia coli in older men, Chlamydia or gonococcus in young men
**Exquisitely tender, warm, boggy prostate** on rectal examination
**Fever and flank pain that persist after days of effective antibiotics**
Urine may be bland if the ureter is blocked
Complication of pyelonephritis, stones or diabetes
Fluid collection beside the kidney on CT, which can track along the psoas

idea.rule: Fever + perineal pain + tender boggy prostate = acute prostatitis.
also: Avoid vigorous prostate massage in acute prostatitis (risk of bacteremia)
Fluoroquinolones or trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole penetrate the prostate

set_title: Hirsutism, acne or virilization in a girl or woman: ovary, adrenal or a drug
stem: A 27-year-old woman has had 4 months of deepening voice, facial hair growth and absent periods. Examination shows clitoromegaly. Serum testosterone is 510 ng/dL and DHEA sulfate is normal.
oneliner: 27F + 4 months of deep voice, facial hair and amenorrhea + clitoromegaly + testosterone 510 ng/dL + normal DHEA sulfate → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.A: It produces slow, mild androgen excess; she has **4 months** of virilization with a **testosterone of 510 ng/dL**
whyNot.B: An adrenal source raises **DHEA sulfate**, and hers is **normal**
whyNot.C: It is gradual and mild; her virilization is **rapid** with a **very high** testosterone
whyNot.E: Exogenous androgens suppress endogenous testosterone to **low** levels; hers is **510 ng/dL**

why: Rapid virilization with a very high testosterone means a tumor. DHEA sulfate comes almost entirely from the adrenal, so a **normal DHEA sulfate** puts the source in the ovary: a Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor.

Testosterone

set_title: Periods stopped, with or without milky discharge: pituitary, drug, thyroid, energy deficit or ovary
stem: An 18-year-old woman, a collegiate cross-country runner, has had no menstrual period for 7 months. She has a metatarsal stress fracture and a BMI of 17.2 kg/m². Serum prolactin and TSH are normal, and FSH, LH and estradiol are low.
oneliner: 18F + cross-country runner + amenorrhea for 7 months + metatarsal stress fracture + BMI 17.2 + normal prolactin and TSH + low FSH, LH and estradiol → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.B: It would raise **prolactin**; hers is **normal**
whyNot.C: It raises **FSH and LH** because the ovary stops responding; hers are **low**
whyNot.D: It raises **TSH**; hers is **normal**
whyNot.E: It follows peripartum hemorrhage and lowers **prolactin**; hers is **normal** and she is a lean runner with a **BMI of 17.2**

why: Low body weight and heavy training slow GnRH pulses, so FSH, LH and estradiol fall and periods stop. **Low gonadotropins and estradiol with normal prolactin and TSH in a lean athlete** is functional hypothalamic amenorrhea, and estrogen deficiency weakens bone, giving the stress fracture.

FSH and LH
TSH
Clincher
rows: No drug or thyroid cause; MRI shows a pituitary adenoma; treat with a dopamine agonist
**Dopamine antagonist** (risperidone, metoclopramide); prolactin falls when the drug stops
Raised TRH also stimulates lactotrophs; levothyroxine corrects the prolactin

Postpartum hemorrhage with failure to lactate; low ACTH and cortisol cause orthostasis
Hot flashes and vaginal dryness; the ovary no longer makes estrogen or inhibin

idea.rule: Low FSH and LH in a lean athlete = hypothalamus; high FSH and LH = ovary.
also: Female athlete triad: low energy availability, amenorrhea and low bone density
Treatment is to restore energy balance
Exclude pregnancy, thyroid disease and hyperprolactinemia first

stem: A 37-year-old woman has had no menstrual period for 5 months and has vaginal dryness. A pregnancy test is negative and serum estradiol is low. Primary ovarian insufficiency and functional hypothalamic amenorrhea are both being considered.
oneliner: 37F + amenorrhea for 5 months + vaginal dryness + negative pregnancy test + low estradiol → primary ovarian insufficiency or hypothalamic amenorrhea?
ask: Which single finding favours primary ovarian insufficiency over functional hypothalamic amenorrhea?

whyNot.B: Both leave the woman **hypoestrogenic**; the stem already gives it
whyNot.C: Low estrogen thins bone in **both**, so a low bone density does not separate them
whyNot.D: With low estrogen the endometrium is thin in **both**, so there is no bleed
whyNot.E: It excludes pregnancy in **both** and does not separate them

why: In both conditions estradiol is low, so vaginal dryness and bone loss follow. In ovarian insufficiency the ovary no longer makes estrogen or inhibin, so the pituitary responds with **elevated FSH and LH**; in hypothalamic amenorrhea the gonadotropins are low.

set_title: No periods by 16 or no puberty: ovary, uterus, androgen receptor or hypothalamus
stem: A 19-year-old woman has never had a menstrual period. Her breasts are Tanner stage 5. Pelvic examination shows a short, blind-ending vagina, and ultrasonography shows no uterus. Pubic and axillary hair are Tanner stage 5.
oneliner: 19F + primary amenorrhea + Tanner 5 breasts + blind vagina + no uterus + normal pubic and axillary hair → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.A: Turner syndrome leaves the breasts **undeveloped** and the uterus present; she has **Tanner stage 5 breasts** and **no uterus**
whyNot.B: Androgen insensitivity gives the same blind vagina and absent uterus but **sparse** body hair; hers are **Tanner stage 5**
whyNot.C: Constitutional delay ends in normal puberty with a uterus; she has **no uterus** and a **blind-ending vagina**
whyNot.E: Kallmann syndrome leaves the breasts **undeveloped** with a uterus present; she has **Tanner stage 5 breasts** and **no uterus**

why: Her ovaries are normal and make estrogen and androgens, so the breasts and body hair mature on schedule; only the paramesonephric ducts failed to form the uterus and upper vagina. **Absent uterus with normal pubic and axillary hair** means Mullerian agenesis.

rows: Little or none, since streak ovaries make no estrogen

also: Karyotype is 46,XX and the ovaries are normal

set_title: Breast tissue in a boy or man: puberty, a drug, a tumor or a chromosome
stem: A 14-year-old boy has had bilateral breast enlargement for 5 months. Examination shows a tender, rubbery 2-cm disc beneath each areola. His genitalia are Tanner stage 3, and he takes no medications. A firm, painless 1.5-cm mass is palpable in the right testis.
oneliner: 14M + 5 months bilateral breast enlargement + tender rubbery discs + Tanner 3 + no drugs + firm right testicular mass → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.A: Pubertal gynecomastia has **normal** testes; his right testis has a **firm mass**
whyNot.B: Klinefelter syndrome has **small, firm testes** bilaterally; his right testis holds a **1.5-cm mass**
whyNot.D: Drug-induced gynecomastia needs a medication; he **takes none**
whyNot.E: Pseudogynecomastia is soft fat with **no firm disc**; he has a **rubbery disc beneath each areola**

why: Germ cell tumors secrete hCG, which acts on LH receptors and raises estradiol, and Leydig cell tumors secrete estrogen directly. A **firm, painless testicular mass with gynecomastia** points to a testicular tumor.

head: Breast exam
Testes
Hormones
Setting
rows: Bilateral, tender, rubbery disc under the areola
High FSH and LH, low testosterone
Any age; germ cell or Leydig cell tumor

**Hard, fixed, painless mass off-center**; nipple retraction or bloody discharge
Older man; BRCA2 or Klinefelter syndrome raises risk

idea.rule: Gynecomastia with a testicular mass: tumor secreting hCG or estrogen; normal testes in a midpubertal boy: pubertal gynecomastia.
also: hCG is the marker for choriocarcinoma and some germ cell tumors
Scrotal ultrasonography is the first test

set_title: Breast tissue in a boy or man: puberty, a drug, a tumor or a chromosome
stem: A 67-year-old man has noticed a lump in his left breast for 2 months. Male breast cancer and gynecomastia are both being considered.
oneliner: 67M + left breast lump for 2 months → male breast cancer or gynecomastia?
ask: Which single finding favors male breast cancer over gynecomastia?

whyNot.A: The stem already gives a lump in the **left breast** only, and gynecomastia is often **unilateral** too
whyNot.B: Tenderness is typical of **gynecomastia** and suggests a benign glandular disc
whyNot.C: Normal testes fit **either** diagnosis, and neither is excluded by it
whyNot.D: The stem already gives **age 67**, and gynecomastia occurs in older men too

why: Gynecomastia forms a symmetric disc centered under the nipple, whereas cancer forms a **hard, fixed mass off-center from the nipple**, often with retraction or bloody discharge. A mass like that needs mammography and biopsy.

idea.rule: Breast lump in a man: hard, fixed and off-center means cancer (biopsy); central, rubbery and tender means gynecomastia.
also: BRCA2 mutation and Klinefelter syndrome raise the risk
Most tumors are ductal and hormone receptor positive

set_title: Sudden severe upper abdominal pain in an adult: the pancreas, a perforation, the gut arteries or a rupture
stem: A 28-year-old woman comes to the emergency department with sudden severe abdominal pain, nausea and lightheadedness. Pulse is 122/min, blood pressure is 84/50 mm Hg, and the abdomen is tender with guarding. Ruptured ectopic pregnancy and acute pancreatitis are both being considered.
oneliner: 28F + sudden severe abdominal pain + nausea + pulse 122 + BP 84/50 + guarding → Ruptured ectopic pregnancy or pancreatitis?
ask: Which single finding favours ruptured ectopic pregnancy over acute pancreatitis?

options.A: Positive hCG with an empty uterus on ultrasound
options.B: Tachycardia and a systolic blood pressure of 84 mm Hg
options.C: Abdominal tenderness with guarding on palpation
options.D: Leukocytosis with a mild fever of 38 C
options.E: Nausea and vomiting with the onset of pain

whyNot.E: Nausea occurs with **either** condition and is in the stem
whyNot.B: Severe pancreatitis can also cause **shock**, and both are in the stem
whyNot.C: Peritoneal irritation from blood or from enzymes causes **guarding** in both
whyNot.D: Fever with a **raised white count** fits pancreatitis at least as well as a bleed, so it does not favour the ectopic

answer: Positive hCG with an empty uterus on ultrasound
why: Hemoperitoneum and pancreatic inflammation can both give shock, guarding and vomiting, so the exam does not decide. **A positive hCG with an empty uterus** shows a pregnancy outside the uterus, usually in the fallopian tube, that has ruptured.

set_title: Malformed brain or spine in a fetus or newborn: which neural tube or posterior fossa defect
stem: A newborn girl is examined in the delivery room. A sac containing spinal cord and nerve roots protrudes through a defect in the lumbar midline. A radiograph of the lumbosacral spine shows defective vertebral arches.
oneliner: Newborn girl + lumbar sac holding spinal cord and nerve roots + defective vertebral arches → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.A: Spina bifida occulta leaves skin intact with no herniated tissue; here a **sac contains spinal cord and nerve roots**
whyNot.B: Dandy-Walker malformation is a posterior fossa cyst in the head; this newborn has a **sac in the lumbar midline**
whyNot.C: Anencephaly is a missing skull vault; this newborn has a **lumbar sac**
whyNot.E: Chiari II malformation is the hindbrain defect that accompanies this lesion; the abnormality described is a **lumbar sac holding cord and roots**

why: Failure of the posterior neuropore to close lets the cord and nerve roots herniate in a sac, which raises maternal alpha-fetoprotein and causes leg weakness and a neurogenic bladder. **A sac containing spinal cord and nerve roots** is myelomeningocele.

Neural tissue exposed

also: Posterior neuropore closes at about day 28

Folate before conception lowers the risk

set_title: Vaginal discharge or itching: read the pH, the smell and the wet mount
stem: A 24-year-old woman has a malodorous vaginal discharge. The discharge has a pH of 5.0, and a wet mount shows squamous cells coated with small bacteria and few white cells.
oneliner: 24F + malodorous discharge + pH 5.0 + bacteria-coated squamous cells, few white cells → ?
ask: What is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.A: Candidiasis gives a thick, odorless discharge with a normal pH and pseudohyphae; her discharge is **malodorous with a pH of 5.0**.
whyNot.B: Lactational atrophic vaginitis causes dryness with little or no discharge; she has **a malodorous discharge with bacteria-coated cells**.
whyNot.D: Trichomoniasis shows motile flagellated organisms with many white cells; her wet mount has **bacteria-coated squamous cells and few white cells**.
whyNot.E: Chlamydia trachomatis cervicitis causes a mucopurulent discharge with many white cells; her wet mount has **few white cells and bacteria-coated squamous cells**.

why: Loss of lactobacilli lets Gardnerella and anaerobes overgrow, which raises the pH and releases amines. **Squamous cells coated with bacteria (clue cells) and few white cells** identify bacterial vaginosis. Treat with metronidazole.

stem: A 31-year-old woman has 2 weeks of itching and burning with a frothy, yellow-green vaginal discharge. Pelvic examination shows a cervix with small punctate red spots.

whyNot.B: Bacterial vaginosis gives a thin gray discharge with little itching or inflammation; she has **a frothy yellow-green discharge with itching and a spotted red cervix**.
whyNot.C: Chlamydia trachomatis cervicitis causes a mucopurulent discharge with a friable cervix; she has **a frothy yellow-green discharge with punctate red spots**.
whyNot.D: Lactational atrophic vaginitis causes dryness without discharge; she has **a frothy yellow-green discharge and burning**.
whyNot.E: Candidiasis gives a thick, white, odorless discharge; hers is **frothy and yellow-green with punctate cervical spots**.

stem: A 32-year-old woman at 33 weeks' gestation has sudden heavy vaginal bleeding. On examination, her uterus is soft and nontender.

whyNot.B: Ovarian fibroma is a benign tumor whose hallmark is ascites with a pleural effusion; she has **vaginal bleeding after menopause with no ascites**

stem: A 71-year-old man has had 3 years of weak urinary stream, hesitancy and nocturia. He has no fever. Rectal examination shows a diffusely enlarged, smooth, firm and nontender prostate.
